description: Dispatcher for the generic logs-*-* index template, which covers Custom Logs datasets and anything an application writes directly. Three jobs: give every document an event.dataset and data_stream.*, route it to its dataset's parser, and normalise severity casing across every producer.

dot_expander.description: Turn flat dotted keys into real nested objects. The elastic ecs-logging-* libraries emit {"log.level":"WARN"} where Spring Boot's own encoder emits {"log":{"level":"WARN"}}. Elasticsearch indexes both identically, but _source keeps whichever form arrived — so without this, later processors here address ctx.log.level and miss the flat key entirely, and Discover shows two different shapes for the same field.

script.description: Backfill event.dataset and data_stream.* from the data stream name. Elastic Agent sets both itself; an application writing straight to _bulk sets neither, and Logstash sets only event.dataset. Without them the document is invisible to dashboards that group by source. During ingest _index is the data stream name (logs-<dataset>-<namespace>), not the backing index, so it parses cleanly.
script.source: def idx = ctx['_index']; if (idx == null || !idx.startsWith('logs-')) { return; } def body = idx.substring(5); int cut = body.lastIndexOf('-'); if (cut <= 0) { return; } def ds = body.substring(0, cut); def ns = body.substring(cut + 1); if (ds.isEmpty() || ns.isEmpty()) { return; } if (ctx.data_stream == null) { ctx.data_stream = ['type': 'logs', 'dataset': ds, 'namespace': ns]; } if (ctx.event == null) { ctx.event = [:]; } if (ctx.event.dataset == null) { ctx.event.dataset = ds; }

lowercase.description: Normalise severity casing. ECS permits the original casing, so ecs-logging-java writes WARN while Elastic Agent and the parsers here write warn. log.level is a keyword and keyword queries are case-sensitive, so without this every dashboard and alert would have to match both spellings — and would quietly miss one.
